podcast-dannyjones-xqIf5y7SaD0:
Exorcist Bob Larson joins Danny Jones to talk about aliens, demons, drugs, and the true origin of Satan. The episode title bills Larson as the world's top exorcist. He has cast out demons on stage and screen for years.

Larson argues that so-called aliens are demons in a new mask. He ties drug use to open doors for dark powers, as he sees them. Jones asks how he tells a demon from a sick mind. Listeners get spiritual war talk from a man who claims the front line. The library holds the episode as an archive record of his beliefs.
podcast-joerogan-W7zfnNH1GD0:
Graham Hancock's episode 551 of the Joe Rogan Experience is an early full statement of his lost-civilization case on the show. Hancock had been arguing for decades that orthodox history misses a fallen, advanced culture. Rogan gave the idea its biggest platform yet.

He lays out the pattern he sees: flood myths on every continent, monuments too skilled for their supposed builders, and a comet strike to end it all. Rogan asks the starter questions that later visits would refine. The episode is a foundation document for the ancient-mysteries arc that became central to the show's identity.
podcast-joerogan-huJVFuLmpd0:
Boxing champion Terence Crawford is the guest on episode 174 of the JRE MMA Show with Joe Rogan. Crawford, one of the finest pound-for-pound fighters of his era, moved between weight classes collecting titles. Rogan's MMA show gives combat greats a fighter-to-fighter stage.

Crawford talks training, focus, and the craft behind his calm, ruthless style in the ring. He explains how he reads opponents and switches stance mid-fight. Rogan, a lifelong martial artist, digs into the mental side of the sweet science. Fight fans get a pugilist's wisdom delivered as calmly as he throws a counter.
podcast-tuckercarlson-4v1XdBi0pd0:
Tucker Carlson asks why the Secret Service will not protect Robert F. Kennedy Jr. Kennedy ran for president outside the two main parties. Candidates in his spot, Carlson notes, often got guards in past races.

He recalls that Kennedy's father and uncle were both shot dead. That history, he argues, makes denial of guards cruel. The episode questions who decides which lives get state protection. It frames the choice as political, not routine. Listeners get a pointed case that a famous name and a real threat should have settled the matter at once.
